messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — noticed inconsistent client-facing codes when requests are routed to fallback pool. Some SDK users see 422 when we soft-fallback, others get 503. We should define a single contract and add console helptext for the fallback UX. Repro steps: small traffic spike -> routing policy moves to fallback model -> some clients get model-validation 422, others get transient 503.

Ajay Patel: I think we mixed two signals: validation vs routing. Proposal: keep validation errors as 4xx (400/422) with explicit error.code field; routing/availability should be 503 (transient) + header that explains fallback. That keeps retriable vs non-retriable semantics clear. :+1:

Ajay Patel: Suggested mapping (short):
- 400/422 = request malformed or model-specific refusal (client should not retry without change)
- 429 = quota exceeded (client may backoff)
- 503 = routing/availability/fallback (client can retry with backoff)
- 500 = internal server error (investigate)

Ajay Patel: For rollout: add header `x-rw-fallback` with values `none|model-mismatch|capacity-fallback|regional-fallback`. Console shows human-friendly hint when header != none. Example response headers:

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-rw-fallback: capacity-fallback
x-rw-request-id: req_abc123
x-rw-quota-remaining: 42
```

Kevin O'Neill: Telemetry note — we need to emit a stable event `route.fallback` with tags: `reason`, `from_model`, `to_model`, `tenant_id`, `route_policy`. That lets SRE/dashboarders slice by cause and surface frequent fallbacks in the console. Also add metric counter `fallback.v1.total` and histogram for fallback latency penalty.

Sarah Liao: Console copy suggestion for the per-route hint: "Requests to this route are temporarily served by a fallback model. This may affect latency and output characteristics. See details and rollback options." Put a small chevron link: "What changed?" linking to the rollout timeline and matching logs. Keep the hint collapsed by default.

Maria Chen: @Ajay — can we make header backwards compatible? i.e., default header absent => old behaviour. New SDKs parse header and show a soft badge in-place, older SDKs ignore. For hosted API, console should map header -> severity badge: capacity-fallback => yellow badge with explanatory tooltip.

Ajay Patel: Yes. Implementation plan:
1) server: always set `x-rw-fallback` when we return 503 due to routing.
2) server: do NOT change validation 422 semantics.
3) console: when seeing `x-rw-fallback`, show hint + link to `insights/fallbacks?route=...`
4) SDKs: add helper `isRetriable(response)` that checks status + header (example below).

Ajay Patel: SDK snippet (JS):
```
function isRetriable(res){
  if(res.status === 503) return true;
  if(res.status === 429) return true; // quota -> backoff
  return false;
}
```

Kevin O'Neill: Also add telemetry mapping so console can surface "top fallbacks" per customer and per model. Make sure we sample full request traces for 1% of fallbacks to get prompt+output diffs.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollout/fallback-header-v1 -> staging successful (link: https://deploys.redwood.example/rollout/fallback-header-v1) :rocket:

Maria Chen: Can we get an eng-runbook checklist before prod deploy? Items: doc update (API docs + SDK changelog), console hint UX, metrics dashboard tile, canary config (5% traffic), rollback playbook. I can own doc + canary.

Sarah Liao: I'll draft the console hint copy + tooltip text and add screenshots to the PR. Also want a small keyboard nav focus state for the hint.

Ajay Patel: I'll add header emission + tests. Will open PR with unit + integration tests for header present/absent and mapping matrix.

Kevin O'Neill: I'll add telemetry event + Grafana panel for `fallback.v1.total` and a dashboard row that shows top tenants by fallback rate.

Maria Chen: Great. Let's meet briefly at 11:15 to align on rollout timing. If no objections, we'll go to canary tomorrow. :thumbsup:
_meta: topic: client-facing error taxonomy and console messaging
